newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends steady, gains vs forward dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends steady, gains vs forward dollar.

text.p: The rupee ended steady at 35.845/855 against the dollar in the spot market on Wednesday but gained against the forward dollar, dealers said.
They said the rupee gained to 35.83 around noon from 35.84/85 opening but reverted to the opening level after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened.
The rupee saw its peak at 35.830 and its weakest point at 35.855 on Wednesday, dealers said.
The RBI continued to defend the dollar, buying both spot and forward dollars, they said. RBI bought spot dollars at 35.84.
In the forwards section, the RBI continued its outright purchases of May dollars, dealers said.
One dealer said RBI's total purchases on Wednesday could be as large as $100 million.

The RBI will continue to intervene to stop the rupee from strengthening but a resulting boost to monetary growth was a constraint, the central bank governor said in an interview to Financial Express newspaper on Wednesday.
He said the central bank was intervening in the currency market in response to a question whether the RBI would help exporters by encouraging a gradual depreciation in the rupee.
"I think this is one action we are taking," he said.
The forward premia looked up after RBI intervened.
The six month annualised premium closed Wednesday at 6.63 percent, up from the previous close of 6.47 percent.
